extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and operational rules for an optional NeurIPS 2026 program giving authors a single, private, automated PAT (Paper Assistant Tool) review of a submission prior to the final deadline. Covers eligibility, submission mechanics, privacy/safety, limitations, and expected behavior of the feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of PAT feedback (issues PAT will flag)
rubrics_metrics.description: The model is designed to help authors identify issues that human reviewers might flag, including (but not limited to) experimental and methodological rigor, narrative clarity in English, and technical correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAT aims to help identify nuanced errors—in proofs, experimental setups, or reasoning—that human reviewers might miss or lack time to detail. The blog notes pilot outcomes (e.g., theory gaps and prompts for new experiments) as examples of the kinds of findings PAT can surface. Authors should treat feedback as actionable suggestions to improve clarity and technical correctness before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact checking and hallucination reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: PAT iteration includes improved search and tool capabilities allowing for fact checking and reducing the hallucination rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This improvement is intended to lower incorrect assertions by the assistant; PAT integrates a ScholarPeer component and other tools to support factual grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related-work comparison capability
rubrics_metrics.description: PAT incorporates a ScholarPeer deep literature review agent so it can compare the submission against related work and take that into account in its analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This empowers PAT to produce feedback that references and situates the paper relative to prior literature, improving the quality of related-work feedback compared to earlier iterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths / Weaknesses analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The feedback produced by PAT will contain an analysis of the potential strengths and weaknesses of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enables authors to improve their paper at a higher level rather than only addressing isolated errors; the tool is tuned to produce higher-level critiques as well as specific comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional program and separation from the official review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is entirely optional, operates inside OpenReview but completely outside the official review process, and the feedback will not be used in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers, area chairs, and program committee members will not have access to PAT feedback, and the PAT system will not be used in any part of the NeurIPS review process (including the AI Assisted Reviewing Experiment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (who may use the program)
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible author is any author whose OpenReview Account was created prior to April 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only eligible authors receive a voucher; attempts by ineligible authors to request PAT review will produce an error and the paper will not be sent for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voucher policy and one-run-per-paper rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each eligible author is granted one virtual 'voucher' to have a single paper run through the AI feedback system; each paper can be run through the system at most once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author who checks the 'Ready for LLM Feedback' checkbox redeems their voucher when the submission edit is submitted. If an author has already used their voucher, selecting the checkbox will fail and the paper will not be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanism: checkbox, PDF upload, and redemption timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors redeem their voucher by selecting a checkbox 'Ready for LLM Feedback' on the OpenReview paper submission form; this only works after a PDF has been successfully uploaded and the version at the time of the edit is sent to the pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checkbox action posts a private author-only comment when the paper enters PAT processing; the voucher is consumed at the edit submission time, so ensure the intended version is uploaded before submitting the edit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program timing window and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: The program runs for a 7 day window ending on the Abstract Deadline (May 4th, Anywhere on Earth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must redeem vouchers during this window. Eligible submissions typically receive feedback within 12 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing affects compute allocation (throttling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted earlier in the feedback window are guaranteed the full compute budget of the PAT pipeline; submissions made very close to the deadline (1-2 days) may be subject to throttling of their overall compute allocation depending on demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This incentivizes earlier submissions to ensure full processing resources; very late submissions risk reduced compute and possibly degraded feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected turnaround time
rubrics_metrics.description: The organizers expect feedback to be posted within 1-2 hours of submission to the PAT system and strive to have all feedback posted within 12 hours of submission; during high demand latency may be longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical expectations (within 12 hours) should guide authors' planning, but be prepared for longer delays near the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF size and content limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to context limitations, very large PDFs (e.g., with multiple high resolution images or plots) may have their images stripped before processing, causing PAT to run only on extracted text; in extreme cases the pipeline may fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend submitting PDFs no larger than 20MB, ideally less than 10MB, to ensure successful processing and preservation of images where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy: strict separation and author-only visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: AI feedback is entirely independent of the NeurIPS review process and is visible only to the authors; reviewers, Area Chairs, and Program Chairs will have no access to this feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This separation is emphasized repeatedly to reassure authors that using PAT will not expose their drafts to reviewers or influence official review decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy: stateless inference (no training on submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve Google’s models; the model operates in a stateless 'inference-only' mode and retains no memory of the specific content for future learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors' text is processed only for immediate feedback generation and is not incorporated into model updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy: data destruction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All PDFs and feedback submitted to Google are stored in a restricted access environment and are scheduled for permanent deletion within 7 days after the feedback is delivered and the program is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy aims to minimize data exposure; authors should note the retention window and that deletion occurs after the feedback delivery plus program completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy: restricted access and explicit-author-approval for inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: No one has access to submission data unless there is a technical difficulty, in which case specified Google staff will only inspect the data (submission PDFs and generated feedback) with explicit author approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named staff (Rajesh Jayaram and Drew Tyler) are indicated as the only ones who may inspect data for troubleshooting, and only after obtaining explicit permission from the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model limitations and author responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Like all LLMs, the models used by the PAT pipeline are not infallible: they may occasionally flag correct statements as errors or miss actual flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should treat generated feedback critically, verify its validity, and consider disagreements as opportunities to add clarification or justification to their paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objective / expected outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary objective is to empower authors to elevate the quality of their submissions by acting as a high-precision filter to catch nuanced errors and help fix clarity and potential technical gaps before peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An anonymous post-program survey will be sent to participating authors (optional) to collect improvement feedback; aggregate results will be shared in the NeurIPS blog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and contact for technical questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical staff will provide limited, best-effort support (e.g., answering questions or checking for failed paper delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should direct questions or feedback to paper-assistant@google.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission success notification
rubrics_metrics.description: After clicking the 'Ready for PAT Review' button, the PDF should be picked up by the PAT system within a few minutes and a private comment (visible only to authors) will be posted notifying that the paper has entered the PAT processing queue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the private comment as confirmation of successful enqueueing; if not posted, contact support.
